clue.text: Well below their prediction?

blocks.note: surface reading: a forecast that fell far short of the mark
setter's reading: people with a forked rod predict where water lies under the ground

explanation.surface: Somebody's forecast turned out to be badly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well below' reads as 'far short of', but a well is a water source lying below the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Water diviners walk fields with a hazel twig and claim to locate underground springs for digging.

clue.text: See 5

blocks.note: surface reading: a cross-reference sending the solver to another clue
setter's reading: this light is the last word of the Shakespeare title clued at 5 down, where Bottom declaims

explanation.walkthrough: This entry completes 5 down's play title; its clue there covers both lights.
explanation.definitionFit: The final word of the title of Shakespeare's comedy of fairies, lovers and mechanicals in an Athenian wood.

clue.text: www.rbrucescave.com ?

blocks.note: surface reading: an internet address, the kind of thing a computer user visits
setter's reading: Robert the Bruce hid in a cave and took heart from a spider patiently spinning its threads there

explanation.surface: A web address for a page about King Robert the Bruce's cave.
explanation.walkthrough: Legend has the Scottish king Robert the Bruce, defeated and hiding in a cave, inspired by a spider trying again and again; the cave is where the web was.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally, it is the location of a spider's web; normally it is an internet page or address.

clue.text: The French had given up gold for this?

definitions.text: The French had given up gold for this?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written from bottom to top

blocks.note: eu is the French past participle of avoir, to have
or is French for gold and the heraldic tincture

explanation.surface: France abandoned its gold-backed money for this new currency.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are French: EU (had) and OR (gold) turned upwards. As a whole, France gave up the franc for this currency.
explanation.definitionFit: France replaced the franc with the single European currency in 2002, giving up its own money.

clue.text: 21s' old cyclic appeal: "O, spend money! A tub, perhaps?"

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters might be arranged some other way

blocks.note: every letter of the quoted phrase

explanation.surface: An old cry urging people to spend money on a tub, perhaps of ice cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is WALL; Wall's is a British ice-cream maker whose tricycle sellers bore the slogan STOP ME AND BUY ONE. A tub is a carton of ice cream.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the famous advertising slogan painted on the tricycles of Wall's ice-cream vendors from the 1920s.

clue.text: Fell from broken window, one's going after the doctor

indicators.note: something broken is smashed apart, so the letters are put back in a new order
one stands for a single letter that is going away, i.e. removed

blocks.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
the word taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Somebody fell from a broken window and a doctor has to attend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' looks like the past of fall, but it is the verb meaning to cut down, as with a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To mow down is to cut or knock people over, as to fell is to bring something crashing to the ground.

clue.text: (and 1) Bottom lines declaimed here

blocks.note: surface reading: the last lines of a page, or a final figure
setter's reading: Nick Bottom the weaver speaks his part in a Shakespeare comedy

explanation.surface: The bottom lines of a text, spoken aloud in some place.
explanation.walkthrough: With 1 down this is A MIDSUMMER NIGHT'S DREAM, where Bottom the weaver is the leading mechanical.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottom is the weaver given an ass's head in Shakespeare's comedy of fairies and lovers.

clue.text: A horse in with a double place in NSW

indicators.note: the article and horse are put inside the following pair of letters

blocks.note: W is short for with
taken as written
gee-gee, a child's word for a horse
taken as written
a double is a second copy, so the five letters just built are written again

explanation.surface: A racehorse in a double event at a New South Wales track.
explanation.walkthrough: The Australian name repeats itself, so the clue builds one half and calls for a copy. NSW is New South Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagga Wagga is a large inland city in the Riverina region of the Australian state New South Wales.

clue.text: One women's movement for social reform

indicators.note: movement suggests shifting about, so the letters are moved around

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A feminist campaign pushing for changes in society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Women's movement' reads as feminism, but 'movement' is the signal. Robert Owen was a Welsh mill owner and utopian socialist.
explanation.definitionFit: Owenism was the nineteenth-century programme of cooperative villages and humane factories devised to improve working lives.

clue.text: No bird left to say "Cheep"

definitions.note: spoken, the bird's call is cheap, an adjective like the answer

blocks.note: taken as written
a variant spelling of myna, an Asian starling
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: There is no bird left to chirp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheep' looks like the bird's call; said out loud it is cheap, which is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominal fee or rent is a token, very small amount of money, hence inexpensive.

clue.text: Blocked classic vessel in ground

indicators.note: the vessel sits in the middle of the word for fixing firmly

blocks.note: to ground something firmly is to fix it in place
Jason's ship in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A famous old ship has run aground and is stuck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' reads as land, but it is the verb: to ground something is to fix it firmly in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that are embargoed are barred from trade by official order, so their movement is blocked.

clue.text: Single ampere shedding light

indicators.note: the phrase sheds its outer letters, leaving a run from the middle

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A tiny electric current gives off a little light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shedding light' looks like one phrase, but 'shedding' is the signal and 'light' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleam is a brief faint shine or glint, a small quantity of brightness.

clue.text: She serves young skate or mother fish

blocks.note: an informal word for mother
the ide, a freshwater fish, is also spelt id

explanation.surface: A waitress offers a menu of skate and other fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Three routes to one word: a female servant, the fishmonger's name for a young skate, and MA + ID.
explanation.definitionFit: A maid is a female household servant, and fishermen call a young skate or thornback ray a maid.

clue.text: Legwork of aunt, a limbo dancer

indicators.note: a limbo dancer twists and contorts, so the letters before are contorted too

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly relative does the limbo, which takes some legwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambulation is the act of walking about, which is literally work done with the legs.

clue.text: Chaps spreading tension among peace-loving Protestants

indicators.note: spreading scatters the letters out into a new arrangement

blocks.note: chaps are men
taken as written

explanation.surface: Men stirring up trouble within a pacifist church.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mennonites are an Anabaptist Christian denomination known for their pacifism and refusal of military service.

clue.text: Given time, he'd have one climbing up the wall

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Given enough time, a man would have one of those creepers covering his wall.
explanation.walkthrough: HEDERA is the botanical genus name of ivy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivy is the classic plant that clings to and scales masonry, and its Latin genus name is used here.

clue.text: High aims rectified French sickness

indicators.note: rectified means put right, so the letters are reset in a corrected order

blocks.note: taken as written
mal is French for illness or pain

explanation.surface: Lofty ambitions put right a French malady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' looks like an adjective for aims; here it means smelly, as meat that is high.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat or game that is high has gone off and smells rank, like the foul vapours of a miasma.

clue.text: Ship's boy so confined?

blocks.note: a room on board a ship
a short boy's name

explanation.surface: A cabin boy, cooped up below decks on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ship's boy' wants to be one unit, cabin boy; split it, and the cabin is the ship's and the boy is ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Shut in a small cabin means cramped and restricted, as in Macbeth's 'cabined, cribbed, confined'.

clue.text: An air of study about Herr Sachs

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the study word goes around the name

blocks.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
Hans Sachs, the cobbler-poet of Wagner's Die Meistersinger

explanation.surface: A tune from a study of the Meistersinger hero.
explanation.definitionFit: A chanson is a French song, and an air is a song or melody.

clue.text: Service producing such ballads on tap?

definitions.text: Service producing such ballads on tap?

blocks.note: surface reading: songs available on demand at any time
setter's reading: the place where drinks from the tap are served and rowdy singing follows

explanation.surface: A service that supplies ballads whenever wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On tap' means available on demand, but here it means draught beer, which fuels the singing.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub's drinking room serves draught beer, and bawdy songs sung there are called by its name.

clue.text: Scourge leaving many sadly wrinkled

indicators.note: the number leaves the word, so its letter is taken away
sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the remaining letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many

explanation.surface: A plague has left many people sadly lined with age.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugose is a botanical and anatomical word for a surface covered with creases or ridges.

clue.text: Thrift making one, say, see red

indicators.note: say means the following word is taken by its sound alone

blocks.note: the verb, spelt as the ocean
a pale shade of red

explanation.surface: Being made to save money makes someone angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thrift' looks like economy and 'see red' like anger; thrift is also a coastal plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrift, or Armeria, is a cliff-top plant with rose-coloured flower heads, also called by this name.

clue.text: A monarch abandoned caution when flying

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase for an adjective meaning to do with flight

indicators.note: abandoned also means wild and unrestrained, so the letters run riot

blocks.note: taken as written
Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
taken as written

explanation.surface: A king or queen threw caution to the wind on taking to the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned caution' reads as reckless, but 'abandoned' is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Aeronautic means relating to the science and practice of air travel, the business of flight.

clue.text: 24's divisive role in 5 1 down's tragedy

blocks.note: surface reading: an actor's part that splits people
setter's reading: in A Midsummer Night's Dream, Snout plays the barrier between Pyramus and Thisbe in the mechanicals' play

explanation.surface: An actor's part in a Shakespeare tragedy that divides the cast.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Snout (24) plays the partition with a chink in the 'tragedy' of Pyramus and Thisbe staged inside A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: A partition built of brick or stone separates two spaces, so it is literally divisive.

clue.text: One's in the right for the rest

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the legal word

blocks.note: a lien is a legal right to keep property until a debt is paid
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone who is in the right gets to have a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside LIEN, after its E.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie-in is a spell of staying in bed later than usual in the morning, a rest.

clue.text: One's beaten the house, some say

blocks.note: first meaning: a percussion instrument struck with sticks
second meaning: slang for a home or flat

explanation.surface: Someone is defeated by the house, as at a casino.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some say' flags the slang sense: in British criminal slang a drum is a house.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a percussion instrument hit with sticks, and old British underworld slang for a dwelling.

clue.text: Tobacco tin discarded

blocks.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
thrown out

explanation.surface: An old tobacco tin has been thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: Snout is British prison slang for tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: Prisoners in Britain use this slang term for cigarettes and loose rolling leaf.

clue.text: Old Testament woman, like Solomon with a difference

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
a pronoun for a woman
King Solomon is proverbial for wisdom

explanation.surface: A biblical woman as sage as Solomon, but different.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherwise means in another way or differently, so something done otherwise is done differently.

clue.text: Indian's bow made with pressed palms

definitions.text: Indian's bow made with pressed palms

blocks.note: surface reading: an archer's weapon, perhaps made from palm wood
setter's reading: a respectful greeting given with the hands held together

explanation.surface: An Indian archer's bow fashioned from flattened palm fronds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow' looks like a weapon and 'palms' like trees; both are the gesture of greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: In India people greet each other with a slight bend of the head and hands held together before the chest.

clue.text: Just a second! I'm making pink champagne for the Raj

indicators.note: making suggests forming something new, so the colour word is refashioned

blocks.note: the abbreviation for second
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A host, busy for a moment, mixes pink bubbly for the colonial set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making pink champagne' reads as one phrase, but 'making' works on the colour alone. The Raj was British rule in India, and this was its Anglo-Indian slang word.
explanation.definitionFit: British India's servants and officers turned the French wine's name into this Anglo-Indian corruption.
